newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP contracts 11 mln T coal to Japan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP contracts 11 mln T coal to Japan.

text.p: Resources and steel group The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had agreed to sell a total of 11 million tonnes of coking coal to Japanese steel mills for the year starting April 1, 1997.
BHP said modest price increases had been achieved at the premium end of the hard coking coal market, while prices for lower quality coals had decreased.

BHP said the agreement involved the delivery to the Japanese Steel Mills of 5.5 million tonnes of hard coking coal and an estimated 5.5 million tonnes of weak coking coal to be finalised with individual steel mills.
"Higher sales of weak coking coal reflect the startup of the Mount Owen and South Walker Creek mines," BHP said.
The company said the settlement was a satisfactory result and provided a solid base for further growth in demand by locking in significant increases in tonnage.

"Again this year, prices and volumes have been aligned to reflect specific coal qualities for each of the coal brands involved, and their suitability to individual customer's needs," said Geoff Lill, BHP Coal's general manager, marketing and transport services.

Lill said the outcome was consistent with the highly competitive nature of current world coal markets, and reflected the difficult economic conditions being experienced in the international steel industry which have impacted on the Japanese Steels Mills.
"The outlook for steel production worldwide is flat, with annual crude steel production in Japan likely to remain unchanged next year, at around 99 million tonnes," he said.
Lill said other world suppliers such as Canada and the U.S. were seeking to increase their share of the Japanese coking coal market.
Japan accounts for around 28 percent of total annual sales from the mines managed by BHP Coal. Other major markets are Europe, Korea, Taiwan, India and South America.

The coal brands involved in the settlement are Peak Downs, Goonyella, Riverside, Saraji, Gregory, Norwich Park, Blackwater and South Walker Creek, all from central Queensland, and Mt Owen from the Hunter Valley of New South Wales.
